  • Orchestrate across the pipeline. Unify recall, ranking, query understanding, and personalization behind one definition of quality and one set of business metrics, so improvements compound instead of colliding.

  • Turn ML research into production wins. Partner deeply with ML and data science to take models — from candidate generation and recall to LLM-assisted interpretation — from idea to production, balancing accuracy, latency, and cost.

  • Make quality measurable and explainable. Build the metrics, evaluation frameworks, and tooling the whole chapter uses to measure, attribute, and explain discovery quality and its business impact.

  • Own quality under pressure. Lead investigation and triage when issues arise, and design durable, systemic fixes rather than one-off patches.

  • Grow the mandate. Expand into chapter-wide leadership spanning ML Recall, ML Infra, and — over time — teams like CORE, SABR, and Catalog Management.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first year, you will have:

  • Driven measurable lift in search-attributed conversion and revenue per visit — moving business metrics, not just quality metrics.

  • Driven measurable business-metric lift (conversion, revenue per visit, GMV) and relevance lift across every major retail vertical we serve.

  • Shipped at least one state-of-the-art ML / LLM-assisted capability into production that beats our previous best on relevance.

  • Fluency with retrieval and recall, query understanding (tokenization, synonyms, spelling correction, multilingual support), and search evaluation frameworks.

  • Excellent cross-functional leadership — able to align teams with different goals behind a shared definition of quality and a shared set of business metrics, working shoulder-to-shoulder with engineering, data science, and ML Ops.

  • Comfort operating with ambiguity, setting direction where none exists yet, and leading through clarity and credibility rather than the org chart.

title: Staff Product Manager: Product Discovery Engine
description:
Staff Product Manager, Product Discovery Engine

About Us

Constructor powers product search and discovery for some of the largest retailers in the world. We serve billions of requests every week, and you’ve probably seen our results somewhere and used our product without knowing it. We differentiate ourselves by focusing on metrics over features, and reinventing search and discovery from the ground up as a machine learning challenge with the specific goal of improving metrics like revenue. We’re approximately doubling year over year despite the market slowing down and have customers in every eCommerce vertical. We’re a passionate team of technologists who love solving problems and want to make our customers’ and coworkers’ lives better. We value empathy, openness, curiosity, continuous improvement, and are excited by metrics that matter. We believe that empowering everyone in a company to do what they think is best can lead to great things.

Job Summary

We’re looking for a systems-minded Staff Product Manager to take Constructor’s search and discovery to the state of the art — and keep it there — across every retail industry we serve. This is a highly technical, high-leverage role at the core of our Product Discovery Engine chapter: the teams responsible for how we retrieve, understand, and rank the right products for every shopper, on every query, for every customer.

Your job is to raise discovery quality and, through it, our customers’ business metrics. You won’t be measured on features shipped — you’ll be measured on relevance and business outcomes, like conversion, revenue per visit, and search-attributed GMV, moving up.

You’ll start embedded with our Search Quality team, owning its strategy and roadmap and getting deep into the systems that decide what shoppers actually see. Over time, your mandate grows to setting direction for the entire Product Discovery Engine chapter — deciding where we’re heading and why across recall, ranking, query understanding, personalization, and the ML infrastructure underneath. This is a Staff role today with a clear path to Director as you take on chapter-wide leadership.

Search at Constructor is fundamentally a machine learning problem, so this role lives and breathes ML. You’ll partner closely with ML, data science, and engineering to turn the latest research into production wins, keep us ahead of both commercial competitors and academic state of the art, and be the connective tissue that aligns multiple teams — ML Recall, ML Infra, and, over time, teams like CORE, SABR, and Catalog Management — behind a single, coherent vision for great discovery.

If you’re excited about driving innovation across dozens of the world’s largest retailers, being held to relevance and business outcomes, and pushing an already best-in-class product further ahead, this role is for you.

What You’ll Do

  • Own business impact, not features. Drive measurable lift in search-attributed conversion, revenue per visit, and GMV alongside relevance across our customer base.

  • Deliver across every retail industry. Move quality and business metrics across all the verticals we serve, accounting for the differences in catalog, language, and shopper intent.

  • Keep us at the state of the art. Continuously translate the latest ML / IR research and competitive moves into production wins, and ship SOTA ML / LLM-assisted capabilities that beat our previous best on relevance.

  • Set chapter vision and strategy. Define the multi-quarter direction for the Product Discovery Engine — where we’re heading and why — tie it directly to customer business outcomes, and rally teams behind it.

  • Lead Search Quality first. Own its strategy and roadmap, driving measurable improvements in the relevance and correctness of results.

  • Orchestrate across the pipeline. Unify recall, ranking, query understanding, and personalization behind one definition of quality and one set of business metrics, so improvements compound instead of colliding.

  • Turn ML research into production wins. Partner deeply with ML and data science to take models — from candidate generation and recall to LLM-assisted interpretation — from idea to production, balancing accuracy, latency, and cost.

  • Make quality measurable and explainable. Build the metrics, evaluation frameworks, and tooling the whole chapter uses to measure, attribute, and explain discovery quality and its business impact.

  • Own quality under pressure. Lead investigation and triage when issues arise, and design durable, systemic fixes rather than one-off patches.

  • Grow the mandate. Expand into chapter-wide leadership spanning ML Recall, ML Infra, and — over time — teams like CORE, SABR, and Catalog Management.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first year, you will have:

  • Driven measurable lift in search-attributed conversion and revenue per visit — moving business metrics, not just quality metrics.

  • Driven measurable business-metric lift (conversion, revenue per visit, GMV) and relevance lift across every major retail vertical we serve.

  • Shipped at least one state-of-the-art ML / LLM-assisted capability into production that beats our previous best on relevance.

  • Won head-to-head quality benchmarks against every major competitor in the verticals we compete in, with a repeatable, defensible methodology.

  • Taken core quality metrics to best-in-class levels and kept them improving quarter over quarter.

  • Stood up an evaluation framework and tooling that ties model and system investments directly to customer business outcomes.

What We’re Looking For

  • Extensive product management experience (typically 8+ years) in search, discovery, ML, or NLP-heavy products, including time operating at a senior or staff level.

  • A track record of moving business metrics at scale — conversion, revenue, engagement — not just shipping features, and of setting strategy across multiple teams.

  • Deep understanding of the end-to-end search pipeline: query interpretation → recall / candidate generation → ranking → reranking → personalization → delivery.

  • Strong ML product depth — owning production models and reasoning about tradeoffs between high-capacity (LLM / batch) and low-latency (real-time) approaches — and a habit of staying current with state-of-the-art research.

  • Fluency with retrieval and recall, query understanding (tokenization, synonyms, spelling correction, multilingual support), and search evaluation frameworks.

  • A rigorous, measurement-first mindset that ties every quality investment back to business outcomes.

  • Excellent cross-functional leadership — able to align teams with different goals behind a shared definition of quality and a shared set of business metrics, working shoulder-to-shoulder with engineering, data science, and ML Ops.

  • Comfort operating with ambiguity, setting direction where none exists yet, and leading through clarity and credibility rather than the org chart.

Benefits

  • Unlimited vacation time — we strongly encourage all of our employees to take at least 3 weeks per year.

  • A competitive compensation package including stock options.

  • Company-sponsored US health coverage (100% paid for employee).

  • Fully remote team — choose where you live.

  • Work-from-home stipend! We want you to have the resources you need to set up your home office.

  • Apple laptops provided for new employees.

  • Training and development budget for every employee, refreshed each year.

  • Parental leave for qualified employees.

  • Work with smart people who will help you grow and make a meaningful impact.

This position is fully remote — Constructor.io is a remote-first company.

Über Hyca Heat

Hyca Heat ist ein deutsches Deep-Tech-Startup an der Spitze der industriellen Energiewende. Wir entwickeln eine weltweit einzigartige, patentierte Heiztechnologie, die hocheffiziente katalytische Verbrennung mit elektrischer Beheizung kombiniert, und dekarbonisieren damit die Prozesswärmeindustrie. Unser Team aus erfahrenen Ingenieuren, Unternehmern und Wissenschaftlern arbeitet in Jülich an einer der größten Herausforderungen unserer Zeit.

Deine Mission

Wir suchen eine:n erfahrene:n Ingenieur:in für die Auslegung und Entwicklung elektrischer Hochtemperatur-Heizsysteme (w/m/d) für unser Team in Jülich. Hybrid-Position mit in der Regel 1–2 Homeoffice-Tagen pro Woche.

Du verantwortest das Herzstück unserer Anlagen: die elektrische Widerstandsheizung unserer Prozessgaserhitzer. Die Besonderheit unserer Technologie: Der Heizleiter ist zugleich die Trägerstruktur des Katalysators – elektrische Beheizung, Wärmeübertragung und katalytische Verbrennung finden in einem einzigen Bauteil statt. Geometrie, Werkstoff, Temperaturprofil und Beschichtung lassen sich nicht unabhängig voneinander optimieren. Genau das macht die Aufgabe anspruchsvoll.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Auslegung elektrischer Widerstandsheizer und Prozessgaserhitzer: Oberflächenbelastung, Heizleitertemperatur, Widerstands- und Leistungsauslegung sowie Wärmeübergang in gasdurchströmten Systemen.
  • Werkstoffauswahl unter realen Atmosphären: FeCrAl und NiCr/Nickelbasis gegen die tatsächliche Gaszusammensetzung – Oxidation, Aufkohlung, Nitrierung, Schwefel- und Wasserdampfeinfluss.
  • Auslegung der Heizleiterstruktur als Katalysatorträger: Zusammenspiel von Geometrie, Oberfläche und Temperaturprofil mit der katalytischen Beschichtung – Beschichtbarkeit, Schichthaftung und Alterung.
  • Thermomechanik und konstruktive Integration: Wärmedehnung und Dehnungsausgleich, Kriechen, Zyklenfestigkeit, Strömungsführung und Vermeidung von Hot-Spots.
  • Erprobung und Systemtests: Prüfstände, Messungen und Schadensanalysen – auch bei Inbetriebnahme und Abnahme beim Kunden – sowie die Auslegungstools und Spezifikationen, mit denen wir künftige Systeme entwickeln.
  • Weiterentwicklung vom Prototyp bis zur Serienfertigung, inklusive Auswahl und Steuerung von Lieferanten.

Was du unbedingt mitbringen solltest

  • Studium oder Technikerausbildung (Bachelor/Master oder Techniker) in Maschinenbau, Verfahrenstechnik, Energietechnik, Werkstofftechnik, Elektrotechnik oder einem verwandten Feld.
  • Industrieerfahrung mit elektrischer Widerstandsheizung: mehrjährige Erfahrung in Auslegung, Entwicklung oder Konstruktion elektrischer Heizsysteme – etwa bei einem Heizleiter- oder Heizelementhersteller, im elektrischen Erhitzerbau oder im Industrieofen- und Thermoprozessanlagenbau.
  • Erfahrung mit Heizleiterstrukturen: Drähte, Bänder, Metallfolien, Netze, Gestruk oder Schäume – du weißt, wie die Bauform auf Oberflächenbelastung, Strömung, Druckverlust und Standzeit durchschlägt. Bei uns trägt genau diese Struktur zusätzlich die katalytische Beschichtung.
  • Werkstoff- und thermomechanisches Verständnis: Du weißt, wie Prozessgase Heizleiterwerkstoffe angreifen, und behandelst Wärmedehnung, thermische Spannungen, Kriechen und Zyklenbelastung als Auslegungsgrößen.
  • Sprachkenntnisse: verhandlungssicheres Deutsch (C1/C2) und sehr gutes Englisch.
  • Offenheit für die Integration und Nutzung von KI-Tools.

Was uns zusätzlich begeistert

  • Erfahrung als Projektleiter:in oder in der Inbetriebnahme beim Kunden.
  • Berufserfahrung mit Brenner-/Heizsystemen, katalytischen Beschichtungen (Washcoat), Wabenkörpern oder metallischen Katalysatorträgern.
  • Kenntnisse in MSR-Technik und Leistungsstellung (Thyristorsteller, Phasenanschnitt, Schwingungspaket).
  • Simulation und Berechnung: FEM/CFD, CAD sowie Python oder MATLAB für Auslegungsrechnungen und Messdatenauswertung.
  • Erfahrung mit Hochtemperaturkorrosion oder mit Schadensanalysen an thermisch belasteten Bauteilen.

  • Act as Flix's in-house SAP expert during the implementation of our new ERP, with a focus on Finance and Procurement. 
  • Translate business requirements from Finance, Procurement and adjacent functions into clean, scalable SAP solutions. 
  • Work closely with external implementation partners during design, build, testing and cut over.

Das Produkt steht. Jetzt entscheidet sich, wie wir darüber sprechen.

Wer wartet, bis jemand den nächsten Schritt vorgibt, auch.

title: Internship - Studio Apelbaum - Art, Engineering or Communication (Berlin)
description:
We are looking for interns in art, engineering, and communication to join Studio Apelbaum.

Studio Apelbaum, founded by artist and engineer Jonathan Apelbaum, combines traditional oil painting with interactive technology to create ‘Cognitive Paintings’ that shift images with light, movement, and sound through custom LED systems and software.

Our team includes engineers, musicians, performers, writers, designers, and builders. We are currently building a new 150 m² studio at Osloer Straße 16–17 in the historic Umspannwerk Christiania, with a workshop and our own exhibition space.

Our own series of invitation-only events and exhibitions is central to the new studio. Over the next few months, we will design and build adaptable furniture in steel and oak so the same room can host work, an exhibition, dinner, and an event.

The whole team is artists in their own way; they think differently and create their own methods.

We create the artworks, design the space, invite our guests, and welcome them. C’est le principe de l’œuvre complète / architecture verticale.

How the internship works

The internship is hands-on and involves working closely with the team across the studio: building, production, and exhibitions.

The first part of the internship will focus on building the new studio, including steel and oak furniture and the adaptable exhibition and dining space. You will then develop the Cognitive Paintings and assemble and test the paintings and their LED systems.

Over the six months, you will take on a main project based on your skills and interests, guided by the team. This could include engineering, programming, communication, music, design, documentation, filming, or any related field.

During the internship, you will gradually develop your own main project based on your skills and interests, in collaboration with Jonathan. This project can develop further and become one of your main areas of work within the studio.

You will also help prepare our major exhibition in May 2027, as well as installations and projects outside the studio with TRACEY (formerly Lunchbox Candy), Playground Festival, and other art festivals.

Tasks

Your tasks will include:

  • Co-building the new studio (steel and oak, as used in the paintings)
  • Co-building, assembling, and testing Cognitive Paintings and their LED systems
  • Organizing materials, tools, storage, artwork transport, and installations
  • Supporting the preparation and installation of exhibitions and events

Depending on your background, skills, and interests, whether in engineering, communication, curation, music, or another field, you will have the opportunity to develop a project that connects with your own passion.

This could include:

  • Contributing to research, prototypes, and software
  • Filming and documenting the studio
  • Designing the exhibition flyers, invitations, and catalog
  • Developing sound or music for exhibitions and events
  • Co-curating exhibitions
  • Exploring new frames, shapes, and materials for the paintings

Requirements

  • A strong interest in art, design, engineering, and communication
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a chosen family
  • Interest in working across different disciplines
  • Reliability, flexibility, and willingness to take initiative
  • A valid driving license is a plus, particularly for assisting with transport, installations, and external projects

Benefits

The internship is part-time, six months, and unpaid.

You don't need a specific background or all the skills listed. You will work closely with a diverse team and learn how to work with electronics, steel, and oak, as well as production and exhibition installation. You will also help prepare and install our main exhibition in May 2027.

Our studio is a place to teach, learn, and grow together. The main project you develop during the internship will be shaped around your own skills and interests and can become the direction of your future work in the studio. We are looking for people who are interested in long-term collaborations.

Please send:

  • CV
  • A portfolio, if available
  • A motivation letter explaining your interest in the studio and the direction you would like to take

title: Senior Social Media Manager (m/w/d)
description:
FlixTrain ist die Challenger-Marke im deutschen Fernverkehr: grün, mutig und anders als der Platzhirsch. Auf Social Media wollen wir genau das zeigen, nicht als Kanäle, die „auch noch mitlaufen", sondern als eigenständige Bühne, auf der unsere Marke für digital-first Zielgruppen erlebbar wird. 

Dafür suchen wir einen Senior Social Media Manager (m/w/d), der Organic Social bei FlixTrain weiterdenkt. Einige Kanäle laufen schon, aber ohne eigene Handschrift. Genau da kommst du ins Spiel: Du machst aus mitlaufenden Kanälen eine eigenständige FlixTrain-Präsenz. Du bekommst einen Startpunkt mit Reichweite, aber freie Hand beim Aufbau von Strategie, Struktur, Prozessen und Partner-Setup. Du entscheidest, wo wir spielen und wo nicht, übersetzt die FlixTrain-Marke plattformgerecht und machst Wirkung messbar. Die Rolle ist Teil des Brand Teams und bewusst als eigenverantwortliche Aufbaurolle angelegt: Du bist In-House-Kopf und Taktgeber, die Produktion steuerst du über Agentur, Creator und internes Creative Team. 

Entscheidend ist eine Haltung: Nähe zum Zeitgeist, ohne jedem Trend hinterherzulaufen. Wir wollen Reichweite mit Substanz: Content, der zur Marke passt, nicht bloße Content-Masse. 

Über die Rolle 

Strategie & Where-to-play 

  • Du entwickelst die Organic-Social-Strategie für FlixTrain: klare Ziele, Zielgruppen und Kommunikations-Säulen: abgeleitet aus der übergeordneten Markenstrategie, nicht als Insel. 
  • Du triffst die Where-to-play-Entscheidung: Du prüfst die bestehenden Kanäle, entscheidest, welche wir fokussieren und welche bewusst nicht, und identifizierst, wo FlixTrain zusätzlich präsent sein sollte. 
  • Du definierst das Zusammenspiel aus „Big Moment"-Ideen (große, reichweitenstarke Momente, die kulturelle Relevanz schaffen) und Ongoing-Community-Content (kontinuierlich, näher an der bestehenden Community)  

Markenübersetzung & Content 

  • Du übersetzt die FlixTrain-Marke plattformnativ – nicht als adaptierten Kampagnen-Cutdown, sondern als eigenständige, kanaltypische Formate, die organisch wirken statt „gebrandet". 
  • Du sorgst dafür, dass Content zum Zeitgeist UND zur Marke passt: Du kombinierst Entertainment- und Kultur-Trends mit echtem Markenfit – kein Trend-Hopping, kein „AI-Slop", kein Content um des Contents willen. 
  • Du betreibst Community Management, hältst die Marke im Dialog präsent und behältst auch bei kritischen Themen einen souveränen Ton – mit dem Gespür, wann ein Fall an PR gehört. 

Partner- & Produktions-Setup 

  • Du baust das richtige Partner-Setup auf und steuerst es. Darüber hinaus managst du das Budget eigenverantwortlich und entscheidest, welche Inhalte gezielt verstärkt werden. 

Measurement & Wirkung 

  • Du machst die Wirkung von Organic Social mit den richtigen KPIs je Zielstellung und Maßnahme messbar — von Big-Moment Content bis hin zu Ongoing-Content — und etablierst ein durchdachtes Reporting, aus dem du gezielt Learnings für die nächste Planungsrunde ableitest. 

Stakeholder & Schnittstellen 

  • Du arbeitest eng mit dem Brand Team, dem FlixBus Social Media Team und dem Creative Team zusammen und sorgst für strategische Konsistenz zwischen Organic, Paid und Kampagne. 
  • Du bist Sparringspartner für interne Stakeholder und externe Partner und vertrittst Social souverän gegenüber Management und Fachbereichen. 

Über Dich 

  • Mindestens 5 Jahre Erfahrung im Organic-Social- bzw. Content-Marketing – idealerweise mit Erfahrung auf Unternehmens- und Agenturseite. 
  • Du bist Generalist: Du denkst strategisch (Where-to-play, KPIs, Positionierung) und bleibst gleichzeitig hands-on in Redaktionsplanung, Briefing und Steuerung. 
  • Du hast Social-Strukturen oder -Kanäle aufgebaut oder maßgeblich geprägt, nicht nur verwaltet – du bringst Ownership und Aufbau-Mentalität mit. 
  • Du bist nah am Zeitgeist und kannst Entertainment-/Kultur-Trends lesen – aber mit dem Urteilsvermögen, sie am Markenfit zu messen und auch Nein zu sagen. 
  • Du steuerst Agenturen, Creator und Freelancer sicher und behältst Budget, Timings und Qualität im Blick. 
  • Du nutzt KPIs, Social Listening und Insights selbstverständlich als Grundlage von Entscheidungen – und erkennst den Unterschied zwischen Reichweite und Wirkung. 
  • Du kommunizierst sicher auf Deutsch und Englisch (jeweils mind. C1-Niveau). 

Bei uns zählt der Blick auf das Ganze – auch wenn du nicht alle Anforderungen zu 100 % erfüllst, aber dennoch glaubst, hier etwas bewegen zu können, freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung. 

Was Wir Bieten 

  • Reisevorteile: 12 kostenlose Flix-Gutscheine + 12 Rabattgutscheine für Freunde & Familie. 
  • Arbeiten von überall: Je nach Rolle bis zu 60 Tage pro Jahr von einem anderen Standort aus. 
  • Hybrides Arbeitsmodell: Bürokultur mit Flexibilität, um Arbeit und Leben in Einklang zu bringen. 
  • Gesundheits- und Wohlfühlangebote: Zugang zu vertraulichen Einzelberatungen, Kursen und Maßnahmen zur Stressbewältigung – für dich und bis zu vier Familienangehörige. 
  • Lernen & Entwicklung: Sprachkurse, Schulungen und Experten-Sessions, um deine Fähigkeiten auszubauen. 
  • Mentoring-Programm: Vernetze dich mit erfahrenen Kolleginnen und Kollegen, um Einblicke zu gewinnen und deine Karriere zu beschleunigen. 

 

Warum Teil von Flix werden? 

Bei Flix konzentrieren wir uns darauf, Reisen einfach, sicher und preiswert zu gestalten – sowohl für unsere Passagiere als auch für unsere Mitarbeiter. Hier geht es schnell voran, und es gibt viel Raum, etwas zu bewegen. Wir wachsen und entwickeln uns täglich weiter und suchen Menschen, die bereit sind, sich einzubringen und die Art und Weise, wie wir arbeiten, mitzugestalten. 

Wenn du einen Job suchst, in dem du wachsen und etwas bewirken kannst, dann bist du bei FlixTrain genau richtig. Hier kannst du Teil eines Teams werden, in dem dein Beitrag zählt und du deine Reise selbst gestalten kannst!

Zip is the AI platform for enterprise procurement — built for humans and agents working together. By orchestrating procurement across teams, tools, and suppliers with the help of AI agents, companies can secure the resources they need to innovate faster than ever before.

The world’s most influential enterprises trust Zip, including T-Mobile, OpenAI, AMD, Mars, Dollar Tree, and more. Together they’ve saved over $8 billion and processed over $500 billion in spend. Your Role

We’re looking for a Solutions Architect to help build the technical foundation that powers Zip’s ERP and integration ecosystem. This role focuses on internal technical enablement, navigating complex customer environments to architect the cleanest possible solutions, partnering closely with Product, and driving best-in-class standards across all of Zip’s integration workflows - with a specific focus on the SAP ecosystem.

As Zip continues to scale rapidly across enterprise customers like Coinbase, Notion, Canva, Samsara, Snowflake, and Databricks, your impact will be foundational: creating reusable integration assets, defining standards of how the Zip product interacts with external systems.

You Will

You’ll work closely with our Engineering, Product, and Design (EPD) teams while reporting to Engineering to design, maintain, and iterate on Zip-owned ERP and integration templates that power scalable, repeatable customer implementations. Your work will directly influence how hundreds of future implementations are delivered, raising the technical bar for both our EPD teams and our customer-facing technical consultant organization.

  • Architect & standardize SAP integrations: Design, build, maintain, and iterate on Zip’s core SAP (ECC and S/4HANA) and Ariba integration templates, ensuring they deliver scalable, repeatable, and robust customer implementations.

  • Bridge product & the field: Work closely with Engineering, Product, and Design (EPD) to ensure integration templates stay perfectly aligned with core product architecture, field insights, and emerging customer needs.

  • Turn nuance into scale: Analyze complex customer implementations to identify reusable data mapping patterns and system nuances, converting bespoke solutions into standardized internal assets.

  • Support pre-sales engineering: Partner with account teams during pre-sales to design and vet integration architectures, ensuring prospective customers are set up for smooth, best-practice deployments.

  • Drive technical implementation excellence: Define, document, and champion technical solution consulting best practices, raising the technical bar and driving consistency across all implementations.

  • Become a Multi-ERP expert: Leverage your existing SAP, P2P, and module expertise (MM/FI) to build deep fluency across additional ERP ecosystems, ultimately becoming the ultimate subject matter expert on integration architecture, data models, and Zip’s App Studio.

You balance high-level architectural design with a willingness to dive directly into API configurations and template modifications to get the job done right.

  • 6+ years of hands-on experience delivering integrations with SAP ERP environments (ECC, S/4HANA) or procurement platforms (Ariba).

  • Experience working with XML / REST based endpoints and standard authentication protocols.

  • Comfortable working with API documentation.

  • Strong communication skills.

Full-cycle recruiting

  • Running multiple searches at once across engineering and non-engineering teams, from intake to accepted offer, prioritised by urgency

  • Coordinating interviews and running debriefs, with blind scorecards in Ashby before any group discussion

  • Building a community of people who know WunderGraph before they ever see a job post

  • Working out what worked, and dropping what didn't

Hiring process

title: GTM DACH
description:
We’re Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years.

To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.

The role

Heidi sits in an unusual position. We lead a category being built for the first time. Hundreds of thousands of clinicians found us on their own, started using the product for free and told a colleague. The market is open and the clinicians in it already like the product. Your job is to turn those smaller scale use cases into enterprise deals.

You're the first line to Heidi in DACH. Inbound demand connects you with practices, MVZs and hospital groups already using us, and you decide whether to qualify each one in, out or close it yourself. Where the signals run thin, you build the outbound.

For most clinicians you'll be the first person from Heidi they ever speak to. You'll both triage inbound to your Account Executive where it belongs and close your own deals from day one, because we want people as close to the frontline as possible. You'll build a network across German-speaking healthcare that outlasts the role.

What you’ll do

  • Work the inbound queue and the warm product signals across DACH. Your day goes to clinicians and practices already using Heidi, where the product tells you who's outgrown the free version.

  • Build outbound where the signals are thin: pick the practice groups, MVZs and hospital groups worth going after and work them in German.

  • Research the accounts behind those signals, work out who else in the practice or hospital group needs to be in the conversation, and build the angle for each one.

  • Reach the people the signals point to, across calls, email and social, while the interest is still fresh.

  • Book demos and meetings for your AEs with enough context that nothing is lost in the handoff.

  • Own small SMB deals end to end, from first conversation through to closed.

  • Keep HubSpot accurate, keep the pipeline moving and hit your qualified-lead number every month.

  • Partner with AEs, Marketing, Product, Operations and Customer Success so what you promise on the call matches what clinicians get, and so the German-language product and collateral keep up with what you hear.

  • Track what's shifting in German healthcare (regulation, the practice groups, the insurers, the competitive set) and tell the team what you're hearing on the phones.

What we're looking for

  • Native or fluent German, and English that allows you to work in a global team.

  • You've worked somewhere with a high bar, whether that's tech, sales, creative, banking, consulting, or PE/VC. We care more about what you've achieved than any time in a sales role.

  • You care about what we do. You'd rather learn how the product works than memorise a pitch.

  • You can hold a conversation with anyone and get to the point of it fast. Clinicians have extremely busy schedules, you respect that and still get the meeting.

  • Knowing how German healthcare buys (who decides in a Praxis, an MVZ or a hospital group, and who pays) is a head start. If you don't know it yet, you're the type who'd learn it in your first month.

  • Organised and self-running. You run your own list, your own day and your own follow-ups without being chased.

  • Passion for AI, shown through hands-on building, prototyping or side projects.

  • You default to building over requesting.

  • You're confident in your thinking and open to being wrong. Great ideas win regardless of who surfaces them.

 

Attitude is more important than experience so if you are a hungry, competitive and highly motivated operator who has a knack for problem solving and building relationships we want to hear from you.

How we show up

  • Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

  • Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

  • Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

  • Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

  • Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

  • Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

Why Heidi?

You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver.

Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it.

True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

We take care of you.

We chose to open-source our benefits hub, if you care to take a peek.

About Superhuman

Grammarly is now part of Superhuman, the AI productivity platform on a mission to unlock the superhuman potential in everyone. Learn more at superhuman.com.

The Opportunity

We’ve consolidated separate compliance programs (Grammarly, Coda, Superhuman Mail, and Superhuman Go) into a single program. We’re rapidly replacing the point-in-time approaches with continuous, automated, code-defined evidence, and this role continues to build on that.

The job is to automate your way out of the manual toil: our GRC automation platform is the evidence-automation backbone, agentic systems (Claude Code and similar) are the force multiplier, and GitHub is where the program lives as code. If your instinct on seeing a manual control-testing process is to turn it into a repeatable, automated pipeline, this role is for you.

What You Will Do:

Configure and operate the GRC automation platform: wire up data sources, build evidence plugins, scope data sets, author analysis rules, and stand up continuous monitoring operations, replacing screenshot-and-upload workflows with automated collectors mapped to controls.

Use Claude Code (or similar) and MCPs for evidence requests, control mapping, gap analysis, vendor reviews, and reporting; build and curate the team’s agent harness; and manage policies, control definitions, and automation in GitHub through branches, pull requests, and review.

  • Design control testing and drive remediation. Instrument testing across SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27017/27018, ISO 27701, PCI DSS, and ISO 42001 for continuous assurance rather than point-in-time snapshots, and work with control owners and engineering to close gaps with automated evidence behind every finding.

You will be configuring our GRC automation platform, not just clicking through it, within your first few weeks. In your first 90 days, we’d expect you to learn the platform configuration, ship your first automated evidence collectors, retire a batch of manual screenshot evidence, and get at least one agent-assisted workflow running end-to-end.

Why This Role:

  • You get the mandate and the tooling to retire manual evidence collection: a GRC automation platform, agentic AI, and compliance-as-code.

  • We actually run LLMs and AI agents in production GRC workflows today. This is how the team operates day-to-day.

  • Small team, high ownership, and a direct line to Legal and Engineering leadership. You’ll shape the program, not just sustain it.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years in compliance, GRC, or IT audit, hands-on with the frameworks above (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and adjacent).

  • Comfortable in GitHub: repos, branches, pull requests, and code review. CI/CD familiarity is a strong plus.

  • Fast on new tooling. You can pick up a GRC automation platform and be productive in weeks, configuring it directly rather than relying on others to do so.

  • Deep GRC fluency: control design, evidence, risk, and how auditors actually think.

  • Working knowledge of cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP): IAM, compute, storage, networking, and security controls, because that’s where the evidence lives.

  • Systems thinker who prefers to automate repetitive manual work rather than repeat it.

Nice to Have:

  • Prior hands-on experience with a GRC automation platform (Vanta, Drata, or similar).

  • Scripting/light coding and API integration experience.

  • Certifications such as CISA, CISSP, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor, or similar.

  • AI governance, AI risk management, or ISO 42001 exposure.

  • Background in a technology, SaaS, or engineering-adjacent environment.

Support for you, professionally and personally

  • Own dangerous goods handling and regulatory compliance, ensuring adherence to ADR, IATA, IMDG, and all relevant legal requirements

  • Ensure that compliance is an integral part of our logistics processes right from the start.

Your Qualifications

  • 6+ years of hands-on experience in logistics or warehouse management, import/export or manufacturing operations

  • At least 4 years of disciplinary leadership and people management experience, ideally with responsibility for teams with 5+ employees

  • Proven expertise in dangerous goods, German regulatory requirements and compliance, ideally combined with cleanroom logistics experience

  • A pragmatic leadership mindset, strategic thinking, and strong problem-solving as well as stakeholder management skills.

  • Fluent German language skills (minimum: C1) and good English (minimum: B2)

Our Work Culture

People Over Processes. At Black Semiconductor, flexibility is key—we ensure work adapts to life, not the other way around. We champion work-life harmony, where careers are meaningful and enriching. Our processes are human-centric, allowing you to focus on what matters.

We Live Openness. Collaboration and inclusivity are the cornerstones of our culture. We practice openness, fostering trust and respect. Individuality is our collective strength, fueling innovation and driving us forward.

Du arbeitest vom ersten Tag an echten Vorgängen, kommunizierst mit Eigentümern, Mietern und Dienstleistern und begleitest Maßnahmen bis zum erfolgreichen Abschluss.

Wir suchen Menschen, die bereits praktische Erfahrungen mit Immobilien, Gebäuden oder immobiliennahen Dienstleistungen gesammelt haben, schnell lernen, selbstverständlich digital arbeiten und richtig Lust haben, sich weiterzuentwickeln.

Aufgaben

  • Du bearbeitest Anliegen von Eigentümern, Mietern und Dienstleistern eigenständig und verbindlich.
  • Du nimmst Schadensmeldungen auf, strukturierst die notwendigen Informationen und koordinierst die nächsten Schritte.
  • Du begleitest Instandhaltungs- und Modernisierungsmaßnahmen.
  • Du beauftragst Dienstleister, holst Angebote und Rückmeldungen ein und behältst Termine sowie Zuständigkeiten im Blick.
  • Du bereitest Entscheidungen vor und verfolgst Vorgänge konsequent bis zum Abschluss.
  • Du arbeitest dich in Objektunterlagen, Verträge und immobilienwirtschaftliche Dokumente ein.
  • Du dokumentierst sämtliche Vorgänge vollständig in unseren digitalen Systemen.
  • Du arbeitest eng mit WEG-Managern, Buchhaltung und technischen Ansprechpartnern zusammen.
  • Mit wachsender Erfahrung übernimmst du zunehmend eigene Verantwortungsbereiche im WEG-Management.

Qualifikation

Immobilienerfahrung ist für uns Voraussetzung – Hausverwaltungserfahrung nicht.

Du musst noch nicht zwingend in einer Hausverwaltung gearbeitet haben. Wichtig ist, dass du die Immobilienwelt bereits aus der Praxis kennst. Deine Erfahrung kann beispielsweise aus der Immobilienvermittlung, Energie- und Gebäudetechnik, einem SHK- oder Handwerksbetrieb, einem Hausmeisterservice, dem Facility Management, dem Schadenmanagement oder einem anderen immobiliennahen Unternehmen stammen.

  • Du hast bereits praktisch mit Immobilien, Gebäuden, Bewohnern, Handwerkern, Schäden oder technischen Maßnahmen gearbeitet.
  • Begriffe wie Teilungserklärung, Wohnungseigentümergemeinschaft, Instandhaltung oder Schadenmeldung sollten dir zumindest grundsätzlich etwas sagen.
  • Du nimmst neue Informationen schnell auf und übersetzt sie in konkrete nächste Schritte.
  • Du arbeitest sehr sicher am Computer und findest dich schnell in neue Programme und digitale Prozesse ein.
  • Du arbeitest strukturiert, dokumentierst zuverlässig und hältst Zusagen sowie Fristen ein.
  • Du kommunizierst freundlich und klar – auch wenn mehrere Vorgänge gleichzeitig Aufmerksamkeit benötigen.
  • Du möchtest Verantwortung übernehmen und dich fachlich zum WEG-Manager weiterentwickeln.
  • Du verfügst über sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift.

Ein vollständiger Quereinstieg ohne bisherigen Bezug zu Immobilien, Gebäuden oder immobiliennahen Dienstleistungen passt für diese Position leider nicht.

Vicoland gives the professional services market a new dimension: Virtual Companies – "Vicos". We invented Vicos as a new type of supplier, more efficient than traditional professional services firms (consultancies, system integrators, agencies etc.). Vicos may consist of freelancers, SMEs and AI agents. They organize through our AI-driven SaaS platform to act like real companies, competing successfully for large enterprise projects, e g. ERP introductions or AI transformations. Vicos have proven to be more cost-efficient and to deliver better quality than traditional companies.

Our certified platform is key to our success. It provides the full digital infrastructure which makes Vicos come true as a new form to organize human labor and human-agentic interaction. It covers end-to-end all essential areas: marketing, finance, legal, and organization.

Given its ambitious and transformative purpose, our platform is highly complex (though easy use). Developing it further takes engineers who combine technical excellence, pragmatic judgement and entrepreneurial spirit. The Tech Lead: AI & Innovation we are looking for embodies these qualities in his or her leadership. He or she is up for making a major contribution to our company and to our society.

Tasks

  • You will lead, grow and enable a team of (forward deployed) engineers: make every engineer successful in their role and hire new ones who strengthen the team.
  • You will be the only (and main) tech lead for the engineering team, with carreer option to progress to CTO
  • Own the technical direction and technology decisions for Vicoland. Set the architecture across the stack, from frontend to infrastructure, and make sure what we build is scalable, robust and maintainable.
  • Stay hands-on: contribute features yourself end-2-end by understanding business needs, coding, building prototypes, and for all that using AI to aggressively ship high-quality software alongside your team.
  • Translate business needs into technical roadmaps in close cooperation with Business Development, Product and other stakeholders. Prioritize, scope and make trade-offs explicit.
  • Makre sure each team member can work end-to-end: concept & design, development, QA, deployment and production monitoring, with clear engineering standards and quality gates.
  • Continuously improve how we build with AI: best practices for context engineering, model selection, evaluation, tracing and observability, so that quality is measured, not assumed.
  • Run architectural discussions, code reviews and retrospectives; create a culture of ownership, constructive challenge and continuous learning.
  • Act as a sparring partner to the Chief Product Officer and the business leadership team on technology strategy, build-vs-buy decisions and team setup.

Requirements

  • Have proven people leadership experience: you have led an engineering team (ideally 3+ engineers), including hiring, performance evaluations, career development and coaching.
  • Have excelled somewhere through an impactful technical contribution, one which we can talk about, and still enjoy writing code yourself.
  • Have deep hands-on experience across the stack (frontend, backend, data, infrastructure/cloud) and a track record of architecting and shipping production-grade software, preferably with AI components (LLMs, embeddings, RAG pipelines, autonomous agents, PyTorch/TensorFlow).
  • Have experience developing AI agents and integrating them into business workflows.
  • Be on top of the latest tools, models and trends in AI-assisted software engineering. You are excellent at context engineering (incl. prompting), know when to leverage which model, and have first-hand experience with Claude Code or Cursor, and you know how to roll these practices out across a team.
  • Know how to evaluate what gets built. You can design eval sets, work with LLM-as-judge or ground-truth data, use tracing and observability tooling to find and fix regressions, and make evaluation a team habit.
  • Practice a truly agnostic approach to stack and tools: you pick the right tech for the problem, not vice versa, and can explain your choices to both engineers and business stakeholders.
  • Balance autonomy and alignment: you drive your team from idea to finished product independently, while knowing when to involve, align with or escalate to others.
  • Have the ability to thoughtfully challenge ideas and drive constructive discussions with users, engineers, product, and business leadership.
  • Lead with humility: you create psychological safety, give and receive honest feedback, and measure your success by the success of your team.
  • Reside within ±3 hours of Central European Time (to enable effective collaboration), at best in one of our office locations in Barcelona, Berlin, Frankfurt, Leipzig, and Sevilla.
  • Full professional proficiency in English at C2 level.
  • Full professional proficiency in German at C1 level.

Bonus Qualifications

  • Experience building or scaling an engineering team in a startup or scale-up environment.
  • Prior experience integrating AI into SaaS business workflows, ideally in a client-facing or forward-deployed setup.
  • Familiarity with the modern AI-tooling ecosystem (agents, memory systems, vector databases, orchestration frameworks).
  • Experience working with distributed or multi-location teams.

Benefits

  • You’ll work in an international, closely knit team of high‑performers and entrepreneurial spirits.
  • Remote‑friendly + flexible work hours.
  • Excellent compensation + participation in the company through our ESOP.
  • Growth mindset: Hard skills are important — but mindset matters more. If you meet most of the requirements and you’re hungry to learn, apply anyway.

If you’re a high‑impact tech lead who thrives on autonomy, drives real results, and is passionate about applying AI to change how teams work - let’s talk. Even if you don’t check every bullet above, but you bring exceptional drive, creativity, and a growth mindset, please apply. We believe the right mindset counts more than checkboxes.

  • Act as the accountable product owner for specific ADAS features, ensuring they are delivered on time, to the agreed specification and in line with customer and business needs.

  • Partner closely with OEM customers to understand their requirements, represent their needs internally and align expectations without compromising Wayve’s product strategy.

  • Work with feature group owners and engineering teams to define feature scope, specifications, performance targets and delivery plans.

  • Engage throughout feature development, providing early feedback, participating in testing and supporting evaluation and validation activities.

  • Identify risks early, manage trade-offs and keep teams aligned as feature requirements, customer priorities and the technology evolve.

  • Owning the end-to-end lifecycle of ADAS features across Collision Avoidance and Lane Keeping, including Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB), Lane Keeping Assist (LKA), Evasive Steering Assist (ESA), Automatic Emergency Steering (AES) and Blind Spot Monitoring (BSM).

  • Defining and evolving feature specifications in partnership with OEMs, engineering and product teams.

  • Harmonising customer requirements across OEM partners to maximise reusable assets, scalability and efficient feature delivery.

  • Setting clear performance targets and ensuring features meet customer requirements, internal capabilities and agreed delivery specifications.

  • Supporting testing, evaluation and validation to ensure feature quality and readiness for production.

  • Maintaining and evolving the strategic feature roadmap as Wayve’s technology advances towards higher levels of autonomy.

  • Participating in agile planning and delivery rituals, helping teams manage dependencies, risks and priorities effectively.

  • Ensuring feature delivery aligns with relevant automotive quality, safety and compliance expectations.

🙌 You should apply if:

  • You have strong experience specifying and delivering ADAS features from concept through to production, particularly across Collision Avoidance or Lane Keeping functions such as AEB, LKA, ESA, AES or BSM.

  • You understand automotive development processes, including requirements management, the V-model, ASPICE, quality and validation.

  • You are confident working directly with OEM customers: understanding their needs, negotiating requirements and representing their perspective internally while maintaining a clear view of Wayve’s product strategy.

  • You have sufficient technical depth to engage credibly with engineering teams on feature trade-offs, feasibility, testing, evaluation and validation.

  • You are a strong cross-functional collaborator who can bridge technical and commercial perspectives, creating alignment across customers, product and engineering teams.

  • You proactively identify risks and issues before they escalate, balancing immediate delivery needs with the longer-term product roadmap.

  • You are comfortable in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment and can bring structure and clarity without adding unnecessary process.

  • Experience shipping complete ADAS features into large-scale automotive production programmes would be valuable.

  • Knowledge of automotive quality, safety and compliance standards—including ASPICE, SOTIF, functional safety, GSR-II and DCAS—would be valuable.

  • Experience with machine learning, LLMs or recent generative-AI methods and architectures would be beneficial.

  • You bring curiosity and a forward-looking approach to developing new ADAS capabilities and advancing the customer experience.

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

This is a full-time role based in our Leonberg office. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces and workshops with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

  • Initial call / recruiter screen (30 minutes)

  • Competency interviews (HM Interview) 45 Minutes

  • Deep-dive technical interviews (ADAS domain knowledge, Technical Depth and Presentation)

  • Final interview: mission & values alignment.

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

title: Systems Integration & QA Engineer (All genders)
description:
About Us

STARK is a new kind of defence technology company revolutionising the way autonomous systems are deployed across multiple domains. We design, develop, and manufacture high-performance unmanned systems that are software-defined, mass-scalable, and cost-effective — providing operators with a decisive edge in contested environments.

We are focused on delivering deployable, high-performance systems — not future promises. In a time of rising threats, STARK is bolstering the technological edge of NATO Allies and their Partners to deter aggression and defend Europe, today.


About the team

Mission Simulation is STARK’s digital proving ground — the tactical environment where our entire ecosystem of UAVs, surface vessels, and EW systems converges. The Mission Simulation team is a small, specialized group based in Munich, working closely with our platform and C2 teams to integrate all multi-domain assets into high-fidelity, Software-in-the-Loop simulators.

We move fast, ship realistic environments, and build for three core purposes: rigorous testing, high-stakes demos, and tactical training. There is no room for gamification. We simulate the reality of combat — from complex swarm logic to EW degradation — ensuring that developers can fail fast, and real soldiers can train safely before hitting the battlefield. 


Your mission

As a Systems Integration & QA Engineer, you are the critical link between our physical simulation hardware and our software development team. You will physically assemble our simulator setups and rigorously test the software environments running on them. By building our QA processes from the ground up, you ensure that every simulation runs flawlessly, and you provide highly detailed, actionable feedback to our software engineers before any system is used for high-stakes training or customer demos.

title: Senior Principal Optical Systems Engineer
description:
We are seeking a Senior Principal Optical Systems Engineer to lead the architecture, design, modeling, integration, characterization, and validation of advanced optical microsystems and photonic test solutions. This senior individual-contributor role owns complex development efforts from concept through production release and applies deep expertise in optics and photonics to resolve multidisciplinary technical challenges.

This is an on-site position based in Karlsruhe, Germany, where Keystone does exciting work on advanced 3D-printed micro-optics and optical probe heads. The role is part of our parent company, FormFactor, and will work in close collaboration with a team on the U.S. West Coast. Candidates should be willing to travel to the U.S. several times per year.

FormFactor, Inc. (NASDAQ: FORM), is a leading provider of essential test and measurement technologies along the full semiconductor product life cycle — from characterization, modeling, reliability, and design debug, to qualification and production test. Semiconductor companies rely upon FormFactor’s products and services to accelerate profitability by optimizing device performance and advancing yield knowledge. The company serves customers through its network of facilities in Asia, Europe, and North America.

Tasks

The successful candidate will provide technical leadership across engineering, manufacturing, quality, software, and commercial teams; translate customer and product needs into system requirements; and establish robust design, simulation, test, and validation methods. This role influences technical roadmaps and engineering practices through expertise and collaboration rather than direct people management.

Optical System Architecture and Product Development

• Lead development of advanced optical systems, micro-optical components, and photonic test solutions from concept through commercial deployment.

• Translate customer, product, and application requirements into system architectures, performance specifications, interfaces, and verification plans.

• Own system-level optical performance and manufacturability, reliability, cost, schedule, and scalability of optical subsystems.

• Drive technical decisions for complex programs with significant ambiguity, multidisciplinary dependencies, and business impact.

• Collaborate closely with Mechanical and Controls engineering teams to integrate optical components into precision alignment systems.

• Select and characterize subsystem optical components including fiber array units (FAUs) and optical connectors.

• Apply structured design reviews, risk assessment, and requirements traceability throughout the product lifecycle.

Simulation, Modeling, and Analysis

• Develop and validate advanced optical models using wave optics, diffraction, beam propagation, and photonic-device simulation methods.

• Perform tolerance analysis, sensitivity analysis, error budgeting, and performance prediction for complete optical systems.

• Correlate simulation results with laboratory measurements, production data, and field performance.

Test, Metrology, and Automation

• Lead development of optical characterization techniques, measurement methods, fixtures, and system-level verification strategies.

• Define automated test and data-acquisition approaches supporting development, manufacturing, and quality assurance.

• Integrate advanced metrology, image processing, and in-line monitoring solutions for process control and performance verification.

• Use statistical analysis and data-driven methods to improve repeatability, capability, yield, and product performance.

Requirements

• Degree or PhD in Optical Engineering, Physics, Photonics, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

• 8+ years of relevant experience in optical-system development, photonics, semiconductor

equipment, or test and measurement. Equivalent combinations of education and industry experience may be considered.

• Deep expertise in wave optics, optical-system analysis, and photonic devices.

• Demonstrated success leading complex technical projects from concept through implementation or product release.

• Strong experience with optical modeling, simulation, tolerance analysis, and experimental correlation.

• Hands-on experience developing and validating optical test and measurement methodologies.

• Proven ability to independently solve complex, multidisciplinary problems and make sound technical decisions with incomplete information.

• Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate complex topics to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

• Experience with silicon photonics, photonic integrated circuits, or wafer-level optical testing.

• Demonstrated experience in optical design and analysis using ANSYS Zemax.

• Knowledge of advanced microfabrication, additive manufacturing, cleanroom, or semiconductor process technologies.

• Experience with precision optical alignment, opto-mechanical systems, packaging, and system integration.

• Programming and automation experience using Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, or similar tools.

• Familiarity with machine vision, image processing, automated inspection, statistical process control, or design of experiments.

Benefits

• Competitive salary and bonus structure.

• The opportunity to work on leading semiconductor test technology in the growing photonics industry.

• A pleasant working environment in Karlsruhe, including access to a canteen.

• A supportive and international team culture.

Rooted in our core values — Focus on the Customer, Ownership & Accountability, Respectfully & Effectively Communicate, and Motivate & Develop People — we foster an environment where diverse perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated. Everyone can make an impact here. Whether it's improving products, supporting customers, or positively influencing peers and the community, the contributions of our people matter.

As part of Wolt's Platform department (Core Group), you'll help improve and automate operations for our storage access platform - our real time database abstraction layer solution designed with scale and resiliency in mind . The product you will build enforces best practices by design, abstracts database infrastructure, and supports Multi-Region architecture through data sharding and replication. You join a team of highly skilled engineers in designing, building and optimizing this platform and ensuring smooth developer onboarding, constant improvement and optimization. 

As an engineer on the Storage access platform team, you'll work on platform features such as UI for developer teams, storage abstraction layer, database automation, client SDK and proxy, Change Data Capture pipelines, caching and ephemeral storage, Hot & Cold storage management and more.

Our humble expectations

  • A strong developer-to-developer mindset, with a genuine enjoyment of building for internal customers and treating other engineers as your primary users.

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with stakeholders and cross-functional teams.
  • A collaborative spirit and experience contributing to diverse and inclusive work environments.

Technical proficiencies:

  • Expertise in NoSQL databases, particularly Cassandra or DynamoDB.

  • Familiarity with SRE principles; however, a background in Backend Development is essential.
  • Practical knowledge of Kubernetes, including EKS, as an end user.

You don't need to tick every box, but if you see yourself in many of these points, we'd love to hear from you!


What we offer

At Wolt, we're committed to building an environment where engineers can make an impact while enjoying meaningful challenges. As a member of the the team you'll enjoy:

We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

Im Mittelpunkt der Position stehen die Prüfung technischer Anforderungen, die Bewertung von Machbarkeiten sowie die Koordination und Begleitung der Projektumsetzung. Sie arbeiten dabei eng mit unseren Kunden, Lieferanten, der Konstruktion und der Fertigung zusammen.

  • Ermittlung von Material-, Fertigungs- und Arbeitsaufwänden

title: Founders Associate (m/w/d)
description:
Bei uns gibt es mehr zu tun als Hände. Wir geben dir Einblick und Verantwortung ab Tag eins, du findest die Lösungen und setzt sie um.

Meerbusch, überwiegend vor Ort mit Flexibilität · unbefristet · Vollzeit · ab sofort

Hier fängt gerade etwas an, und du kannst von Anfang an dabei sein. Du baust mit an Orten, an denen du selbst gern wärst. Hier macht deine Arbeit einen Unterschied, den man sieht, und gute Arbeit wird bei uns anerkannt und bezahlt. Jeder Monat bringt dich ein Stück weiter, mit Menschen, die du magst. Wie groß das wird, liegt an uns.

Worum es geht

Wir sind acht Leute und betreiben Anlagen im Bergischen Land, auf denen rund 350 Menschen ein kleines Haus haben. Gerade bauen wir daneben etwas Neues auf: ein anderes Produkt, neue Orte, eine neue Marke.

Das Problem dabei ist sehr konkret. Der Geschäftsführer verbringt seine Tage mit Betriebskostenfragen und Pächterfällen, statt an dem zu arbeiten, was uns nach vorne bringt. Und unsere beiden Kolleginnen in Verwaltung und Buchhaltung sind die einzigen Menschen für ihre Themen.

Genau da kommst du rein. Nicht als Aushilfe, sondern als der Mensch, der Dinge übernimmt und dann selbst besser macht.

Was du machst

Dein erstes großes Projekt suchst du dir selbst aus. In den ersten zwei Wochen wählst du aus sechs Themen, die uns alle weiterbringen: unser selbst gebautes Verwaltungssystem mit Lovable oder etwas Besserem weiterentwickeln, die Betriebskostenabrechnung durch KI automatisieren, unsere Finanzen strukturieren und auf Optimierungsbedarf analysieren, eine Vertriebspipeline aufsetzen, Abläufe verbessern oder unseren Vermarktungsauftritt bauen. Was nach sechs Monaten fertig sein soll, legen wir gemeinsam fest.

Daneben hältst du den Alltag am Laufen und unterstützt den Geschäftsführer bei unterschiedlichen Projekten. Du wirst seine rechte Hand: Du bereitest Entscheidungen vor, rechnest durch, baust Übersichten wie unser Finanz-Dashboard und die Cashflow-Planung aus, stellst Unterlagen zusammen, fasst nach und bringst Dinge zu Ende, die sonst liegen bleiben.

Und du lernst die ganze Firma kennen. Du arbeitest dich so weit in Verwaltung und Buchhaltung ein, dass du unsere Kolleginnen vertreten kannst, wenn sie im Urlaub sind oder ausfallen. Heute gibt es bei uns für keine Aufgabe eine zweite Person. Und wo du siehst, dass ihnen etwas die Arbeit leichter machen würde, zeigst du es ihnen.

Außerdem hältst du unserer Kollegin oder unserem Kollegen für die Standorte den Rücken frei. Diese Rolle besetzen wir gerade neu: Sie gestaltet unsere Anlagen, richtet Häuser her und verkauft sie. Damit das draußen stattfinden kann, übernimmst du, was daran im Büro anfällt: Termine, Unterlagen, Behördenwege, Nachfassen.

Und die Website gehört dir. Aufbau, Inhalte, Pflege, Weiterentwicklung. Wie die Marke aussieht und klingt, entscheiden wir. Sichtbar machen wirst du sie.

KI ist dabei dein Werkzeug, nicht dein Bonus. Wir arbeiten damit, wo es geht, und erwarten von dir dasselbe.

Und ja, es gibt auch Bürobedarf zu bestellen und die Weihnachtsfeier zu organisieren. Bei acht Leuten macht das jeder mal. Es ist nicht der Kern der Stelle, aber es kommt vor, und wir sagen es lieber vorher.

Was du nicht machst

Bankgespräche führen, Markenentscheidungen treffen, Zahlungen freigeben. Das bleibt im ersten Jahr bei der Geschäftsführung. Vorbereiten und mitdenken wirst du überall.

Wer du bist

Uns interessiert weniger, was du schon gemacht hast, als wie du bist. Ein Studium hilft, ein bestimmtes ist nicht nötig, Berufserfahrung ist kein Kriterium.

Was zählt: Du bist neugierig und lernst schnell. Du kannst mit Technik und mit KI umgehen oder willst es dringend lernen. Du kannst mit Zahlen umgehen und einen Finanzplan lesen, oder du willst es lernen. Du willst verstehen, wie die Finanzen eines Unternehmens wirklich aussehen, und du glaubst keiner Zahl, die du nicht geprüft hast. Du machst Dinge fertig. Du hörst zu und lässt dir etwas sagen, ohne dich klein zu machen. Du sagst Hallo und Tschüss und scheust dich nicht, bei Bedarf auch mal das Telefon in die Hand zu nehmen, um etwas vorwärtszubringen.

Was du bekommst

Einblick in alles. Zahlen, Verträge, Strategie, Personal. Du sitzt neben dem Geschäftsführer und siehst, wie Entscheidungen zustande kommen. Das bekommst du in einem Konzern nach fünf Jahren nicht.

Verantwortung schneller, als dir lieb ist. Bei acht Leuten gibt es keine Warteschleife. Was du kannst, machst du.

Jemanden, der dich coacht. Du wirst nicht ins kalte Wasser geworfen und dann alleingelassen. Wir nehmen uns Zeit, und wir sagen dir ehrlich, was gut läuft und was nicht.

Eine Rolle, die mit dir wächst. Wir wissen heute nicht genau, wo du in zwei Jahren stehst. Das hängt davon ab, was du dir holst.

Wie wir arbeiten

Wir reden Klartext, auch wenn es unangenehm ist. Widerspruch mit Begründung ist willkommen, besonders gegenüber der Geschäftsführung. Wir arbeiten lieber pragmatisch als perfekt. Fehler sind in Ordnung, solange man sie ausspricht und daraus lernt.

Bewerbung

Kein Anschreiben. Und bitte keine Bewerbung, die eine KI für dich geschrieben hat. Wir wollen dich kennenlernen, nicht ein Sprachmodell. Dass du mit KI umgehen kannst, ist uns wichtig, aber im Job und nicht in der Bewerbung.

Eine Sprachnachricht, etwa eine Minute. Erzähl uns von etwas, das du selbst aufgebaut oder organisiert hast, und sag uns, was wir sonst über dich wissen sollten. Einmal einsprechen reicht, wir erwarten kein Tonstudio.

Dazu deinen Lebenslauf, deine Gehaltsvorstellung und einen Satz dazu, wann du könntest.

title: Senior Product Manager

Nucs AI is revolutionizing cancer care through cutting-edge AI and medical imaging technology. Founded in 2024 by a multidisciplinary team of oncologists, AI researchers, and healthcare innovators, we’re tackling one of medicine’s most pressing challenges: the growing demand for accurate, timely cancer diagnostics in the face of rising scan volumes and limited radiologist capacity.

We sit at the intersection of diagnostics and treatment planning—building AI-powered tools at the convergence of medical imaging, radioligand therapy, and artificial intelligence. Starting with prostate cancer and expanding across oncology, we partner with world-leading medical institutions and pharmaceutical companies across the US, Europe, and Australia to bring precision oncology into everyday clinical practice.

Our mission is to enhance diagnostic precision and expand access to expert-level cancer care, improving patient outcomes worldwide. We’re venture-backed, early-stage, and building a team that blends deep clinical expertise with engineering intensity—moving with the rigor the medical field demands and the speed the problem deserves.

The Opportunity

Nucs AI is looking for a Senior Product Manager who thrives at the intersection of complex technology and specialized end-users. You will own critical parts of our product roadmap, translating deep clinical and technical requirements into clear product direction, then driving execution across data, engineering, regulatory, and commercial areas. This is not a role where you manage a feature backlog in isolation; you will be expected to build conviction around what we should build, why, and in what order, and to defend that thinking rigorously.

What You’ll Do

Product Development Support

  • Own the roadmap for one or more product lines (e.g., DeepPSMA, SelectPSMA, TrackPSMA), balancing clinical impact, technical feasibility, and business value.

  • Engage directly with clinicians, nuclear medicine physicians, and oncologists to deeply understand their workflows, pain points, and decision-making processes.

  • Translate ambiguous, technically complex problems into well-structured product requirements and clear success criteria.

  • Develop and articulate a clear product narrative: why this feature matters, who it serves, and how it connects to the broader platform vision.

  • Navigate the regulatory landscape (FDA, CE marking) as a stakeholder, you do not need to be a regulatory expert, but you must understand how regulatory requirements shape product decisions and timelines.

Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Drive cross-functional execution with engineering, AI/ML, clinical, regulatory, and commercial stakeholders, keeping a small team moving fast without sacrificing quality.

  • Contribute to go-to-market strategy, positioning, and customer enablement alongside commercial and clinical teams.

Analytics & Insights

  • Define and track meaningful product metrics; use data and user feedback to inform iteration and prioritization decisions.


What You Bring

  • 3-6 years of product management experience in a B2B or technical environment building products for specialized, professional users (not purely consumer products).

  • Demonstrated ability to manage complex products where the user base has deep domain expertise, e.g., enterprise software, developer tools, scientific instruments, industrial platforms, or similar.

  • Strong conceptual and systems thinking. You can see the big picture, connect disparate inputs into a coherent product thesis, and reason about second-order effects. You don't just execute, you think.

  • Startup or high-growth experience. You have worked in an environment where speed, ambiguity, and wearing multiple hats were the norm, not the exception.

  • Excellent communication skills. You can write clearly, present a compelling argument, and facilitate productive discussions with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Comfort with technical depth. You do not need to write code, but you should be able to engage meaningfully with engineers and data scientists on architecture, data, and tradeoff discussions.

  • Intellectual curiosity and learning agility. You pick up new domains quickly and enjoy becoming a quasi-expert in areas you previously knew nothing about.

  • Fluency in English (native or professional proficiency required - C1 level or higher)

Bonus Points

  • Experience in healthcare, medtech, health-AI, or a regulated industry.

  • Familiarity with medical imaging, oncology workflows, or clinical decision support.

  • Experience working with AI/ML-driven products where model behavior shapes the user experience.

  • Exposure to FDA 510(k), De Novo, or CE marking processes for software as a medical device (SaMD).

Why Nucs AI

  • Mission with real impact  – Your work directly improves how cancer patients are diagnosed and treated.

  • Ground-floor opportunity  – Early-stage company, meaningful equity, and outsized influence on the direction we take.

  • World-class collaborators  – Work alongside leading oncologists, nuclear medicine physicians, and AI researchers globally.

  • Massive market tailwinds  – Radioligand therapy and AI-driven oncology are multi-billion dollar growth markets.

  • Autonomy and flexibility  – Remote-first, flexible working. We hire great people and trust them to deliver.

  • Equity upside  – Competitive equity package. We’re building something big and want you to share in it.

Submit your resume and a brief note on why this role and Nucs AI excite you.

Dein Profil

description:
About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. This role will be a key contributor to the team and will be responsible for building the tax data operations function for our Deliveroo and Wolt legal entities.  This includes building and operating the data pipelines and infrastructure that power tax analytics and support decision-making across the company.

As DoorDash continues to grow its global footprint across multiple business lines, we are looking for a candidate with experience working with Tax teams to gather requirements, and designing scalable data processes to support them.. This person will grow our unique community via your blend of tax, data technology, and process improvement experience.
